hypotheses.title: Options Breakeven 180-Day Dispersion Cauchy Reversion
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Open-interest weighted breakeven price across combined puts and calls (option_breakeven_180) reflects aggregate institutional pricing expectations. The relative percentage distance (option_breakeven_180 - close) / close measures divergence between options market pricing and spot equity levels. Normalizing against market-cap weighted benchmark dispersion, scaling by 80-day volatility, and mapping through heavy-tailed Cauchy quantiles captures institutional volatility mispricing with low friction.
confounders: Unusually deep out-of-the-money open interest skewing the weighted breakeven average
Corporate dividend announcements altering forward option pricing
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails during prolonged gamma-squeeze regimes where spot continuously expands past breakeven without mean reversion.

candidates.expression: ob_dist = (option_breakeven_180 - close) / close; mean_ob = group_mean(ob_dist, rank(ts_mean(cap, 25)), market); disp_ob = abs(ob_dist - mean_ob) / (abs(ob_dist) + abs(mean_ob) + 0.05); disp_smooth = ts_mean(disp_ob, 80); ob_std = ts_std_dev(ob_dist, 80); adj_ob = disp_smooth * ob_std * ob_dist; adj_mean = ts_mean(adj_ob, 80); adj_std = ts_std_dev(adj_ob, 80); bonus = zscore(adj_mean) + zscore(adj_std); signal = -quantile(bonus, driver="cauchy"); ts_decay_linear(signal, 80)

hypotheses.title: Options Put/Call Volume 90-Day Flow Dispersion Cauchy Reversion
hypotheses.economic_rationale: The 90-day put-to-call options trading volume ratio (pcr_vol_90) quantifies institutional hedging flows versus speculative upside demand. When an equity's options flow deviates excessively from the market-wide cap-weighted put/call volume baseline, institutional hedging reflects extreme sentiment imbalances. Scaling by 80-day volume volatility, standardizing dual moments, and applying a Cauchy quantile inversion extracts an ultra-low-turnover contrarian sentiment premium.
confounders: Systemic macroeconomic index put buying distorting single-stock volume signals
hypotheses.falsification_test: Inverts during catastrophic structural balance-sheet defaults where elevated put volume is fundamentally justified.

candidates.expression: pcr_v = pcr_vol_90; mean_pcr = group_mean(pcr_v, rank(ts_mean(cap, 25)), market); disp_pcr = abs(pcr_v - mean_pcr) / (abs(pcr_v) + abs(mean_pcr) + 0.1); disp_smooth = ts_mean(disp_pcr, 80); pcr_std = ts_std_dev(pcr_v, 80); adj_pcr = disp_smooth * pcr_std * pcr_v; adj_mean = ts_mean(adj_pcr, 80); adj_std = ts_std_dev(adj_pcr, 80); bonus = zscore(adj_mean) + zscore(adj_std); signal = -quantile(bonus, driver="cauchy"); ts_decay_linear(signal, 80)

hypotheses.title: Realized 150-Day Volatility Dispersion Cauchy Reversion
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Realized close-to-close volatility over 150 calendar days (historical_volatility_150) reflects prolonged fundamental uncertainty. Individual equities with extreme positive dispersion relative to market-cap weighted benchmark volatility suffer from excessive retail risk aversion and temporary discount rates. Smoothing with 80-day linear decay and compressing via Cauchy distribution quantiles harvests the low-volatility / volatility-reversion anomaly with minimal turnover friction.
confounders: Permanent secular business model deterioration causing structural volatility shifts
Penny stock trading illiquidity inflating close-to-close variance
hypotheses.falsification_test: Underperforms during sustained high-volatility market crashes where high realized volatility persists across quarters.

candidates.expression: hv = historical_volatility_150; mean_hv = group_mean(hv, rank(ts_mean(cap, 25)), market); disp_hv = abs(hv - mean_hv) / (abs(hv) + abs(mean_hv) + 0.05); disp_smooth = ts_mean(disp_hv, 80); hv_std = ts_std_dev(hv, 80); adj_hv = disp_smooth * hv_std * hv; adj_mean = ts_mean(adj_hv, 80); adj_std = ts_std_dev(adj_hv, 80); bonus = zscore(adj_mean) + zscore(adj_std); signal = -quantile(bonus, driver="cauchy"); ts_decay_linear(signal, 80)
